reasoning: The extract sets out some monitoring and evaluation plans for the high needs element of the funding formula. It says "The EFA will monitor historic spend year-on-year and will challenge Section 251 returns where spend is not reducing as expected", which is a monitoring measure with a defined indicator (spend reduction). It commits to a review after four years, looking at the formula's factors, whether it should reflect actual local authority spending, and whether particular approaches secure "better outcomes for young people, and better value for the taxpayer". It also says "We are planning research on the costs and outcomes resulting from different types of provision, which will inform a review of the factors in the high needs funding formula after four years", and that evidence will be gathered on investment that improves outcomes into adulthood. The last line commits to reviewing the equality assessment in light of consultation responses and monitoring impact under the public sector equality duty. This reaches level 2: there are success measures (outcomes, value for money, spend trends), planned research and a review with a four-year timetable, and use of consultation. The strongest counter-example is that the outcome measures are broad and not specified, and there is no pre-implementation testing or explanation of why it is not needed. It does not reach level 3 because it does not explain why these evaluation approaches were chosen, and it does not say how or when the results of the monitoring, research and review will be published. To reach level 3 it would need to name the specific outcome indicators, justify the evaluation design, and commit to publishing the research and review findings on a timetable.
